title: cljplot2
text:
cljplot2
cljplot2 is a Clojure plotting library rendering static images with clojure2d. A plot is a plain map: data (a sequence of maps), a mapping from data to dimensions, a vector of charts, labels, scales and a theme. There is no DSL and no grammar of graphics: you build and transform the map with ordinary Clojure. Statistics come from fastmath, scales from wadogo.

title: cljplot2
text:
How this book is organised

Use cases - one chapter per family of the R Graph Gallery merged with From Data to Viz: distribution, correlation, ranking, part of a whole, evolution, flow, and colours. Each use case has one canonical example here.
Galleries - figures replicated from other sources: cljplot extras, the lattice book, Vega-Lite and Vega galleries. Figures are reproduced by content (same data, same idea), not pixel by pixel, and link to the use case they illustrate.

Every example names its source and its dataset with the dataset’s licence. All code is Clojure written for cljplot2; no code of the original sources is copied. The datasets are in notebooks/data/ (listed in datasets.edn), not in the library.

title: cljplot2
text:
How to read an example
Each example is the code followed by the image it renders. Examples use these aliases: cljplot2.core as plot (plot/render-image returns a java.awt.image.BufferedImage, which the notebook shows) and cljplot2.chart as chart. Data is read with nu/dataset.

title: cljplot2
text:
A first example: Old Faithful
Waiting time between eruptions against eruption duration (left) and the distribution of eruption durations (right). Two plots sharing one dataset, arranged side by side.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatter, Density. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def faithful (nu/dataset :faithful))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                 :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                 :charts [(chart/scatter)]
                 :labels {:x "eruptions [min]" :y "waiting [min]"}}
                {:data faithful
                 :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density)]
                 :labels {:x "eruptions [min]"}}]
               {:columns 2 :title "Old Faithful geyser"})
 {:width 800 :height 400})

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.1 Violin
Charts of how the values of one numeric variable spread: violins, densities, histograms, boxplots and ridgelines (the R Graph Gallery distribution family), then beeswarms, strip plots, rugs and ECDFs.
Distribution charts put the values on :x and the groups (if any) on :y, so they are horizontal by default. :flip true draws the same plot vertically.
A violin is a kernel density estimate mirrored around the centre line of its group, here with a small box inside (the default :inner).

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.1.1 Basic violin
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
  :charts [(chart/violin)]
  :labels {:title "Sepal length by species" :x "sepal length [cm]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






1.1.2 Ordered violins
levels/order-levels orders the levels by any statistic of a value; the result is the scale’s :domain.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot (reorder). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :petal-width :y :species}
  :scales {:y {:domain (levels/order-levels iris :species :petal-width stats/median {:descending true})}}
  :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :quartiles})]
  :labels {:title "Petal width, species by descending median" :x "petal width [cm]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






1.1.3 Horizontal and vertical
The R Graph Gallery draws violins and boxplots vertically; here that is :flip true on the same plot - values stay on :x, which is now drawn vertically.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal violin plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [p {:data iris
         :mapping {:x :sepal-width :y :species}
         :charts [(chart/violin)]
         :labels {:x "sepal width [cm]" :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc-in p [:labels :title] "horizontal (default)")
                  (-> p (assoc :flip true) (assoc-in [:labels :title] ":flip true"))]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






1.1.4 Violin with a box and sample sizes
Two strip charts share the bands: a violin without inner marks and a narrow box. :n-label writes each group’s count past its largest value.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin with boxplot and sample size. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :site}
  :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :none :color [200 200 220]})
           (chart/box {:width 0.12 :outliers false :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "Barley yield by site" :x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






1.1.5 Grouped violins
A second grouping (here the year, coloured) dodges the violins inside each band, in legend order; with exactly two groups :position :mirror draws split violins, one half per group. The year is a number, so :scales {:color {:type :categorical}} declares it categorical: one colour per year instead of a gradient.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped violin plot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(let [p {:data barley
         :mapping {:x :yield :y :site :color :year}
         :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
         :labels {:x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :none})] :labels {:title "dodged" :x "yield" :y nil})
                  (assoc p :charts [(chart/violin {:position :mirror :inner :quartiles})]
                         :labels {:title "split (:position :mirror)" :x "yield" :y nil})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 550}))






1.1.6 Inner marks
:inner chooses what a violin shows inside: a box (default), quartile lines, a rug or the points. The data is a fixed 5% sample of chem97 (31022 rows), so the rug and the points stay readable.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot; seaborn violinplot (1, 2). Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(def chem97-sample
  "A fixed 5% sample of chem97 (the full data has 31022 rows)."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.05)) chem97)))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [inner [:box :quartiles :rug :points]]
                 {:data chem97-sample
                  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y :score}
                  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
                  :charts [(chart/violin {:inner inner})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":inner " inner) :x "GCSE score"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.2 Density
A kernel density estimate (fastmath) of the values, per panel and group.

1.2.1 Basic density
:bandwidth is a number or a fastmath rule (:nrd0 by default, as R); :kernel any fastmath kernel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density plot. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [[title opts] [["default (:nrd0)" {}]
                                   [":bandwidth 0.1" {:bandwidth 0.1}]
                                   [":bandwidth 0.6" {:bandwidth 0.6}]
                                   [":kernel :epanechnikov" {:kernel :epanechnikov}]]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                  :charts [(chart/density (assoc opts :fill [69 117 180 60]))]
                  :labels {:title title :x "eruption time [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






1.2.2 Mirror density
Two groups, the second drawn downward, with the y = 0 line (:zero-line, on by default). :symmetric puts both halves on one range so they compare by height.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Mirror density chart. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data chem97
                 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :fill :color})]
                 :labels {:title "GCSE score: F up, M down" :x "GCSE score"}}
                {:data chem97
                 :mapping {:x :age :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :symmetric true})]
                 :labels {:title "age, :symmetric" :x "age [months, centred]"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






1.2.3 Several groups
Groups from a colour mapping, overlaid. The line takes the group colour; :fill :color fills each area with its group colour at opacity :alpha, a fixed :fill colour fills every area alike.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density with multiple groups. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:width 2})]
                 :labels {:title "lines" :x "sepal length [cm]"}}
                {:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})]
                 :labels {:title ":fill :color, :alpha 0.4" :x "sepal length [cm]"}}
                {:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:fill [0 0 0 30]})]
                 :labels {:title ":fill [0 0 0 30]" :x "petal length [cm]"}}]
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






1.2.4 Annotated density
Annotation charts take literal positions: a rule at the mean, a text label and a band (chart/rect) over the central 50% of the values.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density chart with annotation. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [xs (map :eruptions faithful)
      mean (stats/mean xs)
      [q1 q3] (stats/quantiles xs [0.25 0.75])]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data faithful
    :mapping {:x :eruptions}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x [q1 q3] :fill [69 117 180 40]})
             (chart/density)
             (chart/rule {:x mean :dash [5.0 3.0] :color :red})
             (chart/text {:x mean :y [:panel 0.95] :text (format "mean %.2f" mean) :anchor [:left :top]
                          :offset [4 0] :color :red})
             (chart/text {:x (* 0.5 (+ q1 q3)) :y [:panel 0.05] :text "IQR" :anchor [:center :bottom]})]
    :labels {:title "Old Faithful eruption times" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))






1.2.5 Small multiples
A facet mapping gives one panel per level; the colour still groups inside each panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density small multiples. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :facet :score :color :gender}
  :charts [(chart/density)]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score by A-level score and gender" :x "GCSE score"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






1.2.6 Stacked density
:position :stack piles the group densities on one common grid; :normalize shows each group’s share.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked density chart. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [p {:data diamonds
         :mapping {:x :price :color :cut}
         :scales {:color {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/density {:position :stack})] :labels {:title ":stack" :x "price [USD]"})
                  (assoc p :charts [(chart/density {:position :normalize})] :labels {:title ":normalize" :x "price [USD]"})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))






1.2.7 Marginal density
:margins adds charts beside the panel: the top margin shares the horizontal axis, the right margin the vertical one. Margin charts read the plot’s data and colour mapping, with :x mapped to the shared dimension for them; they have no axes of their own, so the scatter keeps the only x and y axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal distribution. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter)]
  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})
            :right (chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})}
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals with marginal densities" :x "sepal length [cm]" :y "sepal width [cm]"}}
 {:width 750 :height 650})

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.3 Histogram
Counts of the values in bins shared by all panels and groups.

1.3.1 Basic histogram
:y chooses the bar height: percent of the total (default), count, density (area 1) or probability.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [y [:percent :count :density :pmf]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :waiting}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:y y})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":y " y) :x "waiting [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






1.3.2 Bin size
:bins takes a fastmath estimation rule, a number of equal bins or explicit breaks.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram bin size. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [bins [:sturges 5 40 [1.5 2.5 3.5 4 4.5 5.5]]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins bins})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":bins " bins) :x "eruption time [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






1.3.3 Mirror histogram
Two groups back to back. Bars are filled by the group colour and outlined by :stroke-color - a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill, default); :symmetric gives both halves one range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Mirror histogram. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data chem97 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 30})]
                 :labels {:title "default outline" :x "GCSE score"}}
                {:data chem97 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 30 :stroke-color :white :symmetric true})]
                 :labels {:title "white outline, :symmetric" :x "GCSE score"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






1.3.4 Groups on one axis
:position places the groups’ bars: over each other (translucent), side by side, stacked or normalized.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram with several groups. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [position [:overlay :dodge :stack :normalize]]
                 {:data iris
                  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:position position :bins 15})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":position " position) :x "sepal length [cm]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






1.3.5 Small multiples
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram small multiples. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diamonds
  :mapping {:x :price :facet :cut}
  :scales {:facet {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}
  :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 30})]
  :labels {:title "Diamond prices by cut" :x "price [USD]"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






1.3.6 Marginal histogram
A margin may hold several charts, :size sets its thickness in pixels and :axis true shows the magnitude (count, density) of a histogram or density margin; strips (boxes, rugs, …) work in margins too.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal histogram. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :petal-length :y :petal-width :color :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter)]
  :margins {:top {:charts (chart/histogram {:bins 25 :position :stack :y :count}) :axis true}
            :right {:charts [(chart/box {:outliers false}) (chart/rug)] :size 70}}
  :labels {:title "Iris petals: stacked histogram on top, boxes and a rug on the right"
           :x "petal length [cm]" :y "petal width [cm]"}}
 {:width 750 :height 650})






1.3.7 Strips on a histogram
Any strip chart (box, violin, rug, stripplot, beeswarm, extent) layers on a histogram or density: {:at v} centres it on y = v; :place :bottom draws it below y = 0 in room the chart asks for.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram with boxplot on top; lattice Fig 3.1 (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20}) (chart/box {:place {:at 14.5} :thickness 16})]
                 :labels {:title "box above ({:at 14.5})" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density) (chart/rug {:place :bottom :width 1.0})]
                 :labels {:title "rug below (:bottom)" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density) (chart/stripplot {:place :bottom :rng (r/rng :mersenne 2) :size 6})]
                 :labels {:title "jittered points below" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20}) (chart/beeswarm {:place :bottom :size 4 :bottom-share 0.3})]
                 :labels {:title "beeswarm below" :x "eruption time [min]"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 700})

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.4 Boxplot
A Tukey box per group: quartiles, whiskers to the most extreme values within 1.5 IQR, outliers beyond.

1.4.1 Basic boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :mpg :y :cyl}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Fuel economy by number of cylinders" :x "miles per gallon" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})




The cylinder count is a number, so it is declared categorical - one band per value instead of a numeric axis - with :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}; strings and keywords are categorical by themselves.


1.4.2 Boxplot with jittered points
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with jitter. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :mpg :y :cyl}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:outliers false :color [210 210 225]})
           (chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 7) :jitter 0.2 :size 8 :color [215 48 39 160]})]
  :labels {:title "Box with every car" :x "miles per gallon" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






1.4.3 Group order
Source: R Graph Gallery - Reorder boxplot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety}
                 :scales {:y {:domain (levels/order-levels barley :variety :yield stats/median)}}
                 :charts [(chart/box)]
                 :labels {:title "by median" :x "yield" :y nil}}
                {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety}
                 :scales {:y {:domain (levels/order-levels barley :variety :yield stats/mean {:descending true})}}
                 :charts [(chart/box)]
                 :labels {:title "by mean, descending" :x "yield" :y nil}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






1.4.4 Highlight a group
A derived column and an explicit colour scale: grey for the rest, red for the group in focus. A colour mapping makes groups, and groups inside a band dodge by default; :position :overlay keeps every box on its band’s centre line (each band holds one group anyway).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Highlight a group in boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (map #(assoc % :focus (if (= 6 (:cyl %)) "6 cylinders" "other")) mtcars)
  :mapping {:x :hp :y :cyl :color :focus}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}
           :color {:domain ["other" "6 cylinders"] :range [[190 190 190] [215 48 39]]}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:position :overlay})]
  :labels {:title "Horse power, 6 cylinders highlighted" :x "horse power" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






1.4.5 Grouped boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped boxplot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :site :color :year}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Barley yield by site and year" :x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






1.4.6 Faceted boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot small multiples. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :year :facet :site}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Yield by year, one panel per site" :x "yield" :y nil}}
 {:width 900 :height 500})






1.4.7 Variable width
:varwidth makes each box’s width proportional to the square root of its count.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with variable width. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y :score}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:varwidth true :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score by A-level score" :x "GCSE score" :y "A-level score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 550})






1.4.8 Binned continuous variable
levels/bin cuts a numeric column into half-open interval bins; the bins are ordered levels for the boxes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot from continuous variable. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (levels/bin diamonds :carat {:as :carat-bin :bins [0 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 5.01]})
  :mapping {:x :price :y :carat-bin}
  :charts [(chart/box {:outliers false :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "Diamond price by carat" :x "price [USD]" :y "carat"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






1.4.9 Mean marker
The categorical declaration can also sit on the mapping: (levels/categorical :gear) reads :gear as usual and makes its dimension categorical, here instead of a :scales entry.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with mean. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :qsec :y (levels/categorical :gear)}
  :charts [(chart/box {:mean true})]
  :labels {:title "Quarter mile time by gears, mean marked" :x "quarter mile [s]" :y "gears"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






1.4.10 Sample size
:n-label with :n-format (a format string for the count).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with sample size. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety :color :year}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:n-label true :n-format "%d obs"})]
  :labels {:title "Yield by variety and year" :x "yield" :y nil}}
 {:width 900 :height 650})






1.4.11 Horizontal and vertical
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [p {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :am} :scales {:y {:type :categorical}} :charts [(chart/box)]
         :labels {:x "weight [1000 lbs]" :y "manual transmission"}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc-in p [:labels :title] "horizontal")
                  (-> p (assoc :flip true) (assoc-in [:labels :title] ":flip true"))]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 400}))






1.4.12 Intervals
chart/extent draws an interval per group from fastmath.stats: here the 95% confidence interval of the mean, mean ± standard deviation and a bootstrap percentile interval.
Source: cljplot extents. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [[title opts] [[":ci" {:method :ci}]
                                   [":stddev" {:method :stddev}]
                                   [":bootstrap-percentile" {:method :bootstrap-percentile :rng (r/rng :mersenne 1)}]]]
                 {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :site}
                  :charts [(chart/extent opts)]
                  :labels {:title title :x "yield" :y nil}})
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

title: 1  Distribution
text:
1.5 Ridgeline
Histograms and densities with a categorical :y become ridgelines: one profile per level, growing toward the next level, all on one height scale (:overlap - the tallest profile in band steps).

1.5.1 Basic ridgeline

(def months ["January" "February" "March" "April" "May" "June" "July" "August" "September" "October" "November"
             "December"])

Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline chart. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :mean-temp :y :month}
  :scales {:y {:domain (vec (reverse months))}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Mean temperature in Lincoln, 2016" :x "mean temperature [F]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})






1.5.2 Ridge shapes
Histograms make ridgelines too; any strip chart can share the bands.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline chart. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [p {:data diamonds
         :mapping {:x :price :y :cut}
         :scales {:y {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 40})] :labels {:title "histogram ridges" :x "price" :y nil})
                  (assoc p :data (take-nth 25 diamonds)
                         :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 0.7}) (chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 4) :size 3 :jitter 0.2})]
                         :labels {:title "density ridges with points (4% sample)" :x "price" :y nil})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 550}))






1.5.3 Gradient fill
:fill-gradient colours the area along :x with a clojure2d gradient.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline with gradient. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :max-temp :y :month}
  :scales {:y {:domain (vec (reverse months))}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.5 :fill-gradient :mpl/plasma})]
  :labels {:title "Daily maximum temperature" :x "max temperature [F]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})






1.5.4 Double ridgeline
With two groups, :position :mirror grows the second group away from the next level.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline (two groups). Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y :score :color :gender}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :overlap 0.45})]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score: F up, M down, by A-level score" :x "GCSE score" :y "A-level score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.1 Specifying colours
How cljplot2 picks colours: specifying a colour, palettes, discrete and continuous colour scales, colour in practice and accessibility (the R Graph Gallery colour pages and the data-to-viz colour caveats).
Colours come from clojure2d: any colour name, hex string or RGB(A) vector, about 7,300 named palettes and 5,000 gradients.
A colour is a clojure2d colour: a name keyword, a hex string, an RGB vector, or RGBA with alpha in 0-255.

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.1.1 Calling a colour
Literal rects take a vector of fills, one per interval; the labels are a text chart. :axis false on both scales leaves out axes and grid lines that would mean nothing here.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in base R; colour names (1, 2).

(let [colors [:steelblue :tomato "#2ca25f" "#fdae6b" [102 51 153] [255 0 0 90]]
      labels [":steelblue" ":tomato" "\"#2ca25f\"" "\"#fdae6b\"" "[102 51 153]" "[255 0 0 90]"]
      xs (mapv (fn [i] [i (+ i 0.9)]) (range (count colors)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:scales {:x {:axis false} :y {:axis false}}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x xs :y [0 1] :fill colors})
             (chart/text {:x (mapv #(+ % 0.45) (range (count colors))) :y -0.15 :text labels :size 11})]
    :labels {:title "Names, hex strings, RGB and RGBA vectors" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 900 :height 300}))

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.2 Palettes
Palettes are named lists of colours (c/palette, c/find-palette); gradients are functions of t in [0 1] (c/gradient). A scale’s :range takes either name.

2.2.1 Palette types
Qualitative palettes for categories, sequential for ordered values, diverging around a meaningful middle (here the mean mpg, :midpoint). The lightest end of a sequential palette is almost white and nearly disappears against the grey panel - a property of the palette worth knowing when choosing one.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [mean-mpg (stats/mean (map :mpg mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
      :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/Set2}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "qualitative" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
     {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :petal-length}
      :scales {:color {:range :blues-9}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "sequential" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
     {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :hp :color #(- (:mpg %) mean-mpg)}
      :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :title "mpg - mean"}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})] :labels {:title "diverging" :x "weight" :y "horse power"}}]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 360}))






2.2.2 Palette families
The same scatter with a ColorBrewer, viridis, MetBrewer and Tableau palette. (c/find-palette #"(?i)tableau") lists palettes by name.
Source: R Graph Gallery - paletteer, viridis, RColorBrewer (1, 2, 3). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title palette] [["RColorBrewer Dark2" :RColorBrewer/Dark2] ["viridis" :viridis]
                         ["MetBrewer Klimt" :MetBrewer/Klimt] ["Tableau 10" :tableau-10]]]
    {:data iris :mapping {:x :petal-length :y :petal-width :color :species}
     :scales {:color {:range palette :spread (= palette :viridis)}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
     :labels {:title title :x "petal length" :y "petal width"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 650})




:viridis has 256 colours, so its scale uses :spread true - three colours across the whole palette instead of its first three.


2.2.3 Palette swatches
A palette shown as colours: rects with an identity colour scale (the data values are the colours). Every row is resampled to nine colours with c/resample, which also samples a gradient (given as (c/gradient name)).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Color palette finder.

(let [palettes [[":RColorBrewer/Set2" :RColorBrewer/Set2] [":tableau-10" :tableau-10]
                [":MetBrewer/Hiroshige" :MetBrewer/Hiroshige] [":blues-9" :blues-9] [":viridis" :viridis]
                ["gradient :viridis/magma" (c/gradient :viridis/magma)] [":RColorBrewer/RdBu" :RColorBrewer/RdBu]]
      rows (for [[row [_ p]] (map-indexed vector palettes)
                 [i col] (map-indexed vector (c/resample p 9))]
             {:x0 i :x1 (+ i 0.92) :y0 (- row) :y1 (- 0.85 row) :c col})
      names (for [[row [label]] (map-indexed vector palettes)] {:x -0.2 :y (- 0.42 row) :label label})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:scales {:color {:kind :identity} :x {:domain [-3.6 9] :axis false} :y {:axis false}}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:data rows :mapping {:x0 :x0 :x1 :x1 :y0 :y0 :y1 :y1 :color :c}})
             (chart/text {:data names :mapping {:x :x :y :y :label :label} :anchor [:right :middle] :size 11})]
    :labels {:title "Seven palettes and gradients, nine colours each" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 900 :height 500}))

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.3 Discrete colour scales
Categories take palette colours in level order, unless a scale says otherwise.

2.3.1 Manual colours
A level map as :range gives every level its own colour; a level without one is an error.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
  :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" :darkorange "versicolor" :purple "virginica" :teal}}}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})]
  :labels {:title "Manual colours per species" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






2.3.2 Highlighting a group
One group in colour, the others grey. Cylinder counts are numbers, so the scale is declared categorical.
Source: data-to-viz - The spaghetti plot; don’t use color if it communicates nothing (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :hp :y :mpg :color :cyl}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical :range {4 :lightgrey 6 :firebrick 8 :lightgrey} :title "cylinders"}}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 9})]
  :labels {:title "Six-cylinder cars" :x "horse power" :y "miles per gallon"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






2.3.3 Sequential palettes on categories
A sequential palette has more colours than there are levels: by default the levels take its first colours (all light here, the first nearly invisible on the grey panel); :spread true resamples it across its whole range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - RColorBrewer palettes. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [spread [false true]]
    {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety :color :site}
     :scales {:color {:range :blues-9 :spread spread}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})]
     :labels {:title (if spread ":spread true" "first colours (default)") :x "yield" :y nil}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.4 Continuous colour scales
Numbers on :color get a gradient and a colour bar.

2.4.1 Gradients
:range takes two colours, several colours, a gradient name or any function of t in [0 1].
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2; viridis (1, 2). Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title color-range] [["two colours" [:lightyellow :darkred]]
                             ["four colours" [:lightyellow :orange :red :darkred]]
                             ["gradient name :viridis/magma" :viridis/magma]
                             ["a function: lerp navy to gold" (fn [t] (c/lerp :navy :gold t))]]]
    {:data quakes :mapping {:x :long :y :lat :color :depth}
     :scales {:color {:range color-range}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5})]
     :labels {:title title :x "longitude" :y "latitude"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 700})






2.4.2 Diverging gradient with a midpoint
:midpoint puts a value at the middle of the gradient and scales both sides by the larger distance to it; the colour bar ticks the midpoint. :reverse true turns RdBu around, so high horse power is red.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [mean-hp (stats/mean (map :hp mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :color :hp}
    :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint mean-hp :reverse true}}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 10})]
    :labels {:title (format "Horse power around its mean (%.1f)" mean-hp) :x "weight" :y "miles per gallon"}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))






2.4.3 Reversing
:reverse true turns the colours around: categories keep their order with the colours reversed, a gradient runs the other way.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title color scale] [["categories" :species {:range :RColorBrewer/Set1}]
                             ["categories, reversed" :species {:range :RColorBrewer/Set1 :reverse true}]
                             ["gradient" :petal-length {:range :viridis/viridis}]
                             ["gradient, reversed" :petal-length {:range :viridis/viridis :reverse true}]]]
    {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color color}
     :scales {:color scale}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
     :labels {:title title :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 650})






2.4.4 Binned colours
:kind :binned colours values by bin: a count of equal bins, a breaks vector, or quantile bins ({:quantiles 5}: five bins of about equal counts, an :estimation strategy optional); the colour bar has one block per bin. For a discrete legend of intervals, bin the data with levels/bin, which takes the same :bins.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(def diamonds-sample
  "A fixed 5% sample of diamonds (the full data has 53,940 rows)."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 7)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.05)) diamonds)))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title bins] [["5 equal bins" 5] ["breaks vector" [0 1000 2500 5000 10000 20000]]
                      ["{:quantiles 5}" {:quantiles 5}]]]
    {:data diamonds-sample :mapping {:x :carat :y :price :color :price}
     :scales {:color {:kind :binned :bins bins :range :viridis}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})]
     :labels {:title title :x "carat" :y "price"}})
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

title: 2  Colors
text:
2.5 Colour in practice

2.5.1 Missing values and the theme palette
A missing value gets the theme’s NA colour and the last legend entry; the theme :palette sets the default colours of every plot (here a MetBrewer palette and a magenta NA).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def iris-with-na
  "Iris with every seventh species missing."
  (map-indexed (fn [i row] (if (zero? (mod i 7)) (assoc row :species nil) row)) iris))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data iris-with-na :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "default theme" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
   {:data iris-with-na :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
    :theme {:palette {:color :MetBrewer/Egypt :na [230 0 230]}}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "theme :palette" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 420})






2.5.2 Transparency against overplotting
With 53,940 diamonds the opaque points hide where most of them are; a colour with a low alpha shows the density.
Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title color] [["opaque" [69 117 180]] ["alpha 12 of 255" [69 117 180 12]]]]
    {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :carat :y :price}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4 :color color})]
     :labels {:title title :x "carat" :y "price"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






2.5.3 A line coloured by a variable
A linear or binned colour on a line colours it along its length: each segment takes the colour of the mean of its two ends.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(def lincoln-days
  "Lincoln weather with the day of the year."
  (map-indexed (fn [i row] (assoc row :day (inc i))) lincoln))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title scale] [["gradient" {:range :viridis/inferno}]
                       ["4 bins" {:kind :binned :bins 4 :range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :reverse true}]]]
    {:data lincoln-days :mapping {:x :day :y :mean-temp :color :mean-temp}
     :scales {:color (assoc scale :title "°F")}
     :charts [(chart/line {:width 2})]
     :labels {:title title :x "day of 2016" :y "mean temperature [°F]"}})
  {:columns 1})
 {:width 900 :height 650})

title: 2  Colors
3  Evolution
text:
3.1 Lines
Values over time and other ordered variables: lines, time axes, smoothing and uncertainty, many lines, areas and marks for evolution (the R Graph Gallery evolution pages and the data-to-viz caveats).
Dates are java.time values: a datetime scale places LocalDate, LocalDateTime, Instant and the other temporal types; curves and fits work in epoch milliseconds.
A line joins points in x order; dates on x give a datetime axis.

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.1.1 Basic line with dates
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with ggplot2; Time series (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
  :charts [(chart/line)]
  :labels {:title "Unemployed persons in the US" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






3.1.2 Line styling
Width, colour and points are chart options; :dash mapped to a variable takes the named dash styles in order (:solid, :dashed, :dotted, …), so lines read apart without colour.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with ggplot2 (customization). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1)) economics)
      recent-long (filter #(and (.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1))
                                (#{"psavert" "uempmed" "unemploy"} (:variable %)))
                          economics-long)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data recent :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
      :charts [(chart/line {:width 2 :color [215 48 39]}) (chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [215 48 39]})]
      :labels {:title "width, colour, points" :x nil :y "savings rate, %"}}
     {:data recent-long :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :dash :variable}
      :charts [(chart/line {:width 1.5 :color :black})]
      :labels {:title ":dash by variable" :x nil :y "rescaled"}}]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 400}))






3.1.3 Log scale
Growth at a steady rate is a straight line on a log axis; :sqrt, :pow and :symlog are the other continuous transforms (wadogo scales).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line plot with log scale. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :pce} :charts [(chart/line)]
    :labels {:title "linear" :x nil :y "consumption, billions USD"}}
   {:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :pce} :scales {:y {:kind :log}} :charts [(chart/line)]
    :labels {:title ":log" :x nil :y "consumption, billions USD"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.1.4 Several groups
One line per level of :color; values on different units are rescaled to 0..1 to share an axis.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with several groups. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics-long
  :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :color :variable}
  :charts [(chart/line)]
  :labels {:title "Five economic series, rescaled" :x nil :y "value (0..1)"}}
 {:width 900 :height 450})






3.1.5 Steps and interpolated lines
:interpolator takes any fastmath one-dimensional method: steps, monotone (no overshoot) or cubic curves through the points.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line plot; data-to-viz - Line plot (1, 2). Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [year (filter #(= 1955 (:year %)) air)
      panel (fn [title opts] {:data year :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
                              :charts [(chart/line opts) (chart/scatter {:size 5})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "passengers, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel ":step-after" {:interpolator :step-after})
                  (panel ":monotone" {:interpolator :monotone})
                  (panel ":cubic" {:interpolator :cubic})]
                 {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 350}))






3.1.6 Sampling step
An interpolated line is evaluated every :sample-step pixels (default 1) or at {:count n} positions per run - a coarse count shows the polyline behind a curve.
Source: cljplot2 - line :sample-step. Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [years (filter #(<= 1958 (:year %)) air)
      panel (fn [title step] {:data years :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
                              :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :cubic :sample-step step}) (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "passengers, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel "every pixel (default)" 1) (panel "{:count 12} per run" {:count 12})] {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))






3.1.7 Missing values
A missing (nil) value breaks the line (:gaps :break, default); :gaps :bridge joins the ends with a dimmed segment, so the gap stays visible.
Source: cljplot2 - line :gaps. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [gappy (map (fn [row] (if (<= 1990 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date row)) 1992) (assoc row :psavert nil) row))
                 (filter #(<= 1985 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %)) 1997) economics))
      panel (fn [title gaps] {:data gappy :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
                              :charts [(chart/line {:gaps gaps :width 1.5})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "savings rate, %"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel ":gaps :break" :break) (panel ":gaps :bridge" :bridge)] {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.2 Time axes
Datetime ticks fall on calendar units; the formatter is a function or a java.time pattern string.

3.2.1 Date format and breaks
Source: R Graph Gallery - Time series with ggplot2; Manage dates (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :uempmed}
    :scales {:x {:ticks-params {:unit :years :step 5} :formatter "yyyy"}}
    :charts [(chart/line)] :labels {:title "every 5 years, \"yyyy\"" :x nil :y "weeks"}}
   {:data (filter #(= 2008 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %))) economics) :mapping {:x :date :y :uempmed}
    :scales {:x {:ticks-params {:unit :months :step 2} :formatter "MMM"}}
    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter {:size 5})] :labels {:title "2008, every 2 months, \"MMM\"" :x nil :y "weeks"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.2.2 Time window
An explicit :domain of dates shows one window of a long series; the data outside is clipped by the panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Time series with ggplot2 (select a time frame). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
  :scales {:x {:domain [(LocalDate/of 2000 1 1) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1)]} :y {:domain [4000 16000]}}
  :charts [(chart/line {:width 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Unemployment, 2000-2010" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






3.2.3 Annotations
Literal rects, rules and texts take dates as positions: recessions shaded behind the line, a rule and a label.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart annotation. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [d (fn [y mo] (LocalDate/of (int y) (int mo) 1))
      recessions [[(d 1969 12) (d 1970 11)] [(d 1973 11) (d 1975 3)] [(d 1980 1) (d 1980 7)] [(d 1981 7) (d 1982 11)]
                  [(d 1990 7) (d 1991 3)] [(d 2001 3) (d 2001 11)] [(d 2007 12) (d 2009 6)]]]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data economics
    :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x recessions :fill [0 0 0 35]})
             (chart/line {:width 1.5})
             (chart/rule {:x (d 2008 9) :dash :dashed :color [215 48 39]})
             (chart/text {:x (d 2008 9) :y 14500 :text "Lehman Brothers" :anchor [:right :middle] :offset [-5 0]
                          :color [215 48 39]})]
    :labels {:title "Unemployment and US recessions (NBER)" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






3.2.4 Time heatmap
Year × month as two categorical axes, the value as a linear colour: seasonality and growth at once. A rect whose ends are levels covers the level’s band.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The hourly heatmap. Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [months ["Jan" "Feb" "Mar" "Apr" "May" "Jun" "Jul" "Aug" "Sep" "Oct" "Nov" "Dec"]
      rows (map #(assoc % :year-level (str (:year %))) air)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows
    :scales {:x {:domain months} :color {:range :viridis/viridis :title "passengers"}}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:mapping {:x0 :month :x1 :month :y0 :year-level :y1 :year-level :color :passengers}
                          :stroke-color :white})]
    :labels {:title "Airline passengers by month (thousands)" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.3 Smoothing and uncertainty
chart/smooth fits a curve per group with a band; chart/ribbon draws any band given as :ymin / :ymax.

3.3.1 Smoothers with confidence bands
Loess (default) with nested 50% / 95% bands; a linear model per diet; a Gaussian process (mean ± z·σ). The loess defaults are ggplot2’s geom_smooth ones - 75% of the points, local quadratic fits - with fastmath’s two robustness iterations (:method-params {:iters 0} is ggplot2’s plain fit; the robust bands are a little wider). The bands of the plain fit (:iters 0) equal R’s predict(se = TRUE); with 144 or 220 points they are narrow. On a date axis the fit works in epoch milliseconds - a kernel’s scale too (here three months).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot with ggplot2 (smoothing); Polynomial curve fitting (1, 2). Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [year-ms (* 365.25 86400000.0)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data air :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3}) (chart/smooth {:level [0.5 0.95]})]
      :labels {:title "loess, 50% / 95%" :x nil :y "passengers"}}
     {:data chicks :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
      :labels {:title "lm per diet" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
     {:data (filter #(<= 1956 (:year %)) air) :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
      :charts [(chart/smooth {:method :gp :level [0.5 0.95]
                              :method-params {:kernel (kernel/kernel :gaussian {:sigma (* 0.25 year-ms)})
                                              :noise 0.05 :normalize? true}})
               (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
      :labels {:title "Gaussian process" :x nil :y "passengers"}}]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))






3.3.2 Ribbon
Daily minimum and maximum temperatures as a band, the mean as a line.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Lines with error envelopes. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :date}
  :scales {:x {:formatter "MMM"}}
  :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :min-temp :ymax :max-temp} :color [215 48 39]})
           (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mean-temp} :color [150 30 20]})]
  :labels {:title "Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016: daily min-max and mean" :x nil :y "temperature, F"}}
 {:width 900 :height 420})

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.4 Many lines
Fifty chicks are a spaghetti plot; highlighting, small multiples and labels make it readable.

3.4.1 Highlighting one line
All lines in grey (:group, no colour), then the one of interest from its own :data in colour.
Source: data-to-viz - Spaghetti plot; R Graph Gallery - Highlight elements in a line chart (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chicks
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight}
  :charts [(chart/line {:mapping {:group :chick} :color [190 190 190]})
           (chart/line {:data (filter #(= "21" (:chick %)) chicks) :width 2.5 :color [215 48 39]})
           (chart/text {:data (filter #(= "21" (:chick %)) chicks) :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :label :chick}
                        :select :last :color [215 48 39]})]
  :labels {:title "Chick 21 among all fifty" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






3.4.2 Small multiples with the others greyed
A chart whose mapping sets the facet key to nil is drawn in every panel: all chicks in grey behind each diet’s own.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Small multiple line chart, all groups greyed out. Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chicks
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :group :chick :facet :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:mapping {:facet nil} :color [175 175 175]})
           (chart/line {:color [33 102 172]})]
  :labels {:title "Chicks per diet, all chicks in grey" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






3.4.3 Labels at line ends
chart/text with :select :last keeps one label per series at its last point and makes room for it.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with labels at end of lines. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(and (.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2005 1 1))
                            (#{"pce" "psavert" "unemploy"} (:variable %)))
                      economics-long)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data recent
    :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :color :variable}
    :charts [(chart/line {:width 1.5})
             (chart/text {:mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :label :variable :color :variable} :select :last})]
    :legend false
    :labels {:title "Three economic series since 2005, labelled at the end" :x nil :y "value (0..1)"}}
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






3.4.4 Bump chart
Ranks instead of values: levels/rank-rows ranks the chicks at every weighing (1 - the heaviest; ties by data order with :ties :first), a monotone line joins the ranks on a reversed axis.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic bump plot. Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [eight (set (map str (range 1 9)))
      ranked (levels/rank-rows (filter #(and (eight (:chick %)) (zero? (mod (:time %) 4))) chicks) :time :weight
                              {:ties :first})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data ranked
    :mapping {:x :time :y :rank :color :chick}
    :scales {:y {:domain [8.5 0.5] :nice false :ticks (vec (range 1 9))}}
    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :monotone :width 3})
             (chart/scatter {:size 9})
             (chart/text {:mapping {:x :time :y :rank :label :chick :color :chick} :select :last})]
    :legend false
    :labels {:title "Weight rank of chicks 1-8 on diet 1" :x "days" :y "rank"}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.5 Areas
An area fills between a line and zero, or between stacked lines.

3.5.1 Area chart
Source: R Graph Gallery - Area chart with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Area chart (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
  :charts [(chart/line {:fill :color :alpha 0.4 :width 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Personal savings rate" :x nil :y "%"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






3.5.2 Gradient area
:fill-gradient colours the area along the y (or x) scale’s range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Area chart with gradient. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
  :charts [(chart/line {:fill-gradient [[255 255 255 0] [33 102 172 200]] :fill-gradient-axis :y :width 1.5
                        :color [33 102 172]})]
  :labels {:title "Savings rate, gradient along y" :x nil :y "%"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})





(def diet-means
  "Mean chick weight per diet and day."
  (vec (for [[[diet time] rows] (sort-by key (group-by (juxt :diet :time) chicks))]
         {:diet diet :time time :weight (/ (double (reduce + (map :weight rows))) (count rows))})))



3.5.3 Stacked area
:position :stack aligns the groups on the union of their x values and stacks them; every band is filled.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked area chart; data-to-viz - Stacked area (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diet-means
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:position :stack})]
  :labels {:title "Mean chick weight per diet, stacked" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 800 :height 420})






3.5.4 Percent stacked area
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked area chart (proportion). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diet-means
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:position :normalize})]
  :labels {:title "Share of each diet in the summed mean weight" :x "days"}}
 {:width 800 :height 420})






3.5.5 Stacking order
Groups stack in the colour scale’s order: an explicit :domain reorders the bands (and the legend).
Source: data-to-viz - Stacking caveat; R Graph Gallery - Reorder a variable (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data diet-means :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
    :charts [(chart/line {:position :stack})] :labels {:title "diets 1, 2, 3, 4" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
   {:data diet-means :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet} :scales {:color {:domain ["3" "4" "2" "1"]}}
    :charts [(chart/line {:position :stack})] :labels {:title "diets 3, 4, 2, 1" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.5.6 Streamgraph
Stacked around a moving baseline: :silhouette (symmetric around zero) and :wiggle (least slope); an :interpolator smooths the bands.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Streamgraph; data-to-viz - Streamgraph (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data diet-means :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
    :charts [(chart/line {:position :silhouette :interpolator :monotone})]
    :labels {:title ":silhouette" :x "days" :y nil}}
   {:data diet-means :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
    :charts [(chart/line {:position :wiggle :interpolator :monotone})]
    :labels {:title ":wiggle" :x "days" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.6 Other marks
Segments, candlesticks, colour along a line and paths through time.

3.6.1 Lollipop
A segment from zero to each value ((chart/segment {:yend 0})) under a point, on any x: car models (flipped for readable labels) or dates.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic lollipop plot; data-to-viz - Lollipop (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [ordered (sort-by :mpg mtcars)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data ordered
      :mapping {:x :model :y :mpg}
      :scales {:x {:domain (mapv :model ordered)}}
      :flip true
      :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
      :labels {:title "Fuel economy of 32 cars" :x nil :y "miles per gallon"}}
     {:data (filter #(= 1959 (:year %)) air)
      :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
      :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
      :labels {:title "Passengers in 1959" :x nil :y "thousands"}}]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 700}))






3.6.2 Candlestick
Open-high-low-close per day: the wick from low to high, the body from open to close, green up and red down; OHLC bars as the alternative. The prices are a seeded random walk.
Source: Wikipedia - Candlestick chart.

(def prices
  "Daily open / high / low / close of a random walk over 40 trading days."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 21)
        start (LocalDate/of 2024 3 1)]
    (vec (map-indexed (fn [i close]
                        (let [open (+ close (* 1.2 (r/grandom rng)))
                              spread (m/abs (* 0.8 (double (r/grandom rng))))]
                          {:date (.plusDays start i) :open open :close close
                           :high (+ (max open close) spread) :low (- (min open close) spread)}))
                      (take 40 (reductions + 50.0 (repeatedly #(r/grandom rng))))))))


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data prices :mapping {:x :date :open :open :high :high :low :low :close :close}
    :charts [(chart/candlestick)] :labels {:title "candlestick" :x nil :y "price"}}
   {:data prices :mapping {:x :date :open :open :high :high :low :low :close :close}
    :charts [(chart/candlestick {:style :ohlc})] :labels {:title ":style :ohlc" :x nil :y "price"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.6.3 Line coloured by its value
A linear :color colours the line along its length; binned, it shows ranges (see also the Colors chapter).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line plot colour following y value. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data lincoln :mapping {:x :date :y :mean-temp :color :mean-temp} :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdYlBu :reverse true :title "F"}}
    :charts [(chart/line {:width 2})] :labels {:title "linear" :x nil :y "mean temperature, F"}}
   {:data lincoln :mapping {:x :date :y :mean-temp :color :mean-temp}
    :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdYlBu :kind :binned :reverse true :bins [20 40 60 80] :title "F"}}
    :charts [(chart/line {:width 2})] :labels {:title "binned" :x nil :y "mean temperature, F"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.6.4 Connected scatter
Two variables against each other, joined in time order (:sort false); :curve :bezier passes a smooth path through the points, labels mark some years.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Connected scatterplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Connected scatter (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [yearly (vec (for [[year rows] (sort-by key (group-by #(.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %)) economics))
                        :when (<= 2000 year 2014)]
                    {:year year
                     :uempmed (/ (double (reduce + (map :uempmed rows))) (count rows))
                     :psavert (/ (double (reduce + (map :psavert rows))) (count rows))}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data yearly
    :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert}
    :charts [(chart/line {:sort false :curve :bezier :color [33 102 172]})
             (chart/scatter {:size 6 :color [33 102 172]})
             (chart/text {:data (filter #(#{2000 2003 2006 2009 2012 2014} (:year %)) yearly) :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert :label :year}
                          :anchor [:left :bottom] :offset [4 4]})]
    :labels {:title "Unemployment duration vs savings rate, 2000-2014" :x "median unemployment, weeks" :y "savings rate, %"}}
   {:width 800 :height 550}))

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.7 Functions
chart/function samples functions across the panel. Several functions - a vector, [label f] pairs or a map - are one group each: {:mapping {:color :function}} colours them and gives the legend, labels in the given order. :y-limits keeps asymptotes from flattening the curve (segments across a limit are cut).

3.7.1 Many functions with a legend
Source: cljplot2 - chart/function.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:charts [(chart/function {:f (mapv (fn [k] [(str "sin " k "x") (fn [x] (m/sin (* k (double x))))]) (range 1 11))
                              :domain [0 m/PI] :mapping {:color :function}})]
    :scales {:color {:title nil}}
    :labels {:title "ten [label f] pairs" :x "x" :y "y"}}
   {:charts [(chart/function {:f m/tan :domain [(- m/PI) m/PI] :y-limits [-5 5]})]
    :labels {:title "tan with :y-limits [-5 5]" :x "x" :y "y"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






3.7.2 Parametric curves
:parametric - (fn [t] [x y]) over :t [lo hi], sampled by count; Lissajous figures on an isometric aspect.
Source: Wikipedia - Lissajous curve.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[a b] [[1 2] [3 2] [3 4] [5 4]]]
         {:aspect :iso
          :charts [(chart/function {:parametric (fn [t] [(m/sin (* a (double t))) (m/sin (* b (double t)))])
                                    :t [0 m/TWO_PI] :sample-step {:count 1000}})]
          :labels {:title (str "a = " a ", b = " b) :x nil :y nil}}))
  {:columns 4})
 {:width 1000 :height 300})

title: 3  Evolution
text:
3.8 Caveats

3.8.1 Cutting the y axis; aspect ratio
Starting y at zero shows changes against the whole; a cut axis magnifies them. A wide panel flattens slopes, a narrow one steepens them - the same data.
Source: data-to-viz - Cut y axis; Aspect ratio (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2012 1 1)) economics)
      plot-of (fn [title y] {:data recent :mapping {:x :date :y :pop} :scales {:y y}
                             :charts [(chart/line {:width 1.5})] :labels {:title title :x nil :y "population, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(plot/arrange [(plot-of "y from 0" {:domain [0 330000]}) (plot-of "y cut" {})] {:columns 2})
                  (plot/arrange [(plot-of "wide" {}) (plot-of "narrow" {})] {:columns 2 :widths [4 1]})]
                 {:columns 1})
   {:width 1000 :height 700}))
